text:
sophia_support: Customer EDI-1976 reporting repeated card declines at checkout. UX shows address and CVV entered correctly. Decline messages from our side: 'AVS mismatch' then 'CVV mismatch'. Payment_id: pay_20260315_01, last4: 4242, card_country: US. Happening across 3 different cards and 2 merchant accounts. Can payments/risk take a look?

liam_payments: Looking now — can you paste the raw request/response from the merchant logs (redact PAN) and the upstream auth failure code? @nina_risk FYI.

sophia_support: Pasting redacted snippet from merchant (they attached):
```
POST /v1/payments/pay_20260315_01
body: {
  amount: 12500,
  currency: "usd",
  billing: {
    name: "Jon Perez",
    line1: "123 Main St.",
    line2: "Apt 4B",
    city: "San Jose",
    region: "CA",
    postal_code: "95112",
    country: "US"
  },
  card: { exp: "03/26", last4: "4242" }
}
response: { status: "declined", reason: "avs_mismatch" }
```

liam_payments: Thanks. I pulled the gateway trace for pay_20260315_01. Upstream auth response from acquirer: `auth_result: decline, avs: N, cvv: U` (N = no match, U = unavailable/unchecked). The acquirer then reattempted and returned `cvv_mismatch`.

nina_risk: Two hypotheses: 1) Our address normalization pipeline is altering line2/apartment separator causing issuer to see a mismatch, 2) The card is being routed to a different BIN-country mapping so AVS lookup fails. I can repro locally against the merchant payload.

liam_payments: Repro steps I ran:
1) Send same payload through our sandbox endpoint with exact billing fields.
2) Confirmed normalized payload sent to acquirer: `line1: "123 Main Street"`, `line2: "Apartment 4B"` (our normalizer expands 'St.' -> 'Street' and converts 'Apt' -> 'Apartment').
3) Acquirer trace shows AVS compare against cardholder file: issuer expects `123 Main St Apt 4B` (abbrev) and our expanded `123 Main Street Apartment 4B` flagged as mismatch.

jen_incidents: Interesting — the merchant reported failures only started after we rolled the address-normalizer update last week (release 2026.03.08). Could be regression.

sophia_support: Merchant says they didn't change anything at their end. They started seeing declines 2026-03-10.

liam_payments: Quick mitigation: we can add a merchant-level toggle to send raw billing lines (skip normalization) until acquirer updates mapping. Workaround steps: set `billing.normalize=false` for that merchant via console or API. Would you like me to enable it for merchant id mch_9081?

sophia_support: Please enable it and confirm. Merchant wants a patch ASAP.

liam_payments: Done — toggled `billing.normalize=false` for mch_9081. Will monitor for retries. I also opened a ticket with the acquirer. Ticket ref: ACQ-78642.

billing-bot: [auto] Created escalation ticket ACQ-78642 linking pay_20260315_01 and merchant mch_9081.

nina_risk: I ran a test with normalization off and reprocessed a synthetic auth: acquirer returned `avs: Y, cvv: M` (Y = match, M = match). Looks resolved for the sample.

jen_incidents: Can we get a postmortem/rollback note added to the release? This looks like a behavioral change that impacted AVS strictness.

liam_payments: Agreed. Action items: (1) Keep normalization disabled for mch_9081 until acquirer confirms mapping update. (2) Add a flag to release notes and rollback plan for address-normalizer. (3) Run a quick cohort scan for merchants with >3 declines since 2026-03-10 and enable toggle where necessary. I'll own the acquirer follow-up.

sophia_support: Merchant confirmed 3 successful retries after toggle — they're happy for now. Please update them when acquirer confirms permanent fix. :thumbsup:

jen_incidents: I'll draft a short incident blurb for the next all-hands: root cause = address-normalization expansion; mitigation = merchant-level normalize=false toggle; action = rollout guard + acquirer coordination.

liam_payments: Adding one more note — we should add a regression test: authoritative AVS string equivalence (abbrev vs expanded) for common US address tokens (St, Ave, Blvd, Apt, Unit). Otherwise we may keep breaking issuer comparisons.

nina_risk: Agreed. Also flagging this to product so they can consider exposing normalization settings at merchant onboarding.

sophia_support: Thanks team, closing thread after acquirer ACK.

(reacted :spiral_note_pad: by jen_incidents)
